IS : 9509 - 1980

Indian Standard
GUIDE FOR TREATMENT AND DISPOSAL OF EFFLUENTS OF VISCOSE RAYON INDUSTRY

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 February 1980, after the draft finalized by the Water Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 The rayon industry falls under the group of chemical industries concerned with the manufacture of artificial and synthetic textile fibres. Production of rayon started more than two decades ago and to date there are about ten rayon factories in the country producing 250 tonnes daily of Their gross annual production is about 90 000 tonnes. viscose rayon. 0.3 Rayon is manufacturerd by three different chemical processes, namely the viscose process, the cellulose acetate process, and the cuprammonium In India most of the units produce viscose rayon. process. This guide relates to the treatment and disposal of viscose rayon effluents. 0.3.1 In the case of those units which produce rayon grade pulp according to conventional pulping processes, IS : 5061 ( Part I )-1978* shall also apply. 0.4 Considerable work has been done in this country and abroad on proper treatment and disposal of these effluents and information and data A list of relevant references is given on the subject are now available. in Appendix A for information. These data and information have formed the basis for the preparation of this standard. While realizing that any effluent treatment process has the inherent scope for being further improved, the Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard has given careful consideration to the feasibility of the methods cited in literature and has been of the view that effective measures can now be taken by the industry for abatement of pohution. It is hoped that public health authorities and other agencies concerned with water pollution control in the country will find this standard useful.
*Guide for treatment and disposal of effluents of pulp, paper and board industries: Part I For mills with chemical recovery systems (first revision)

3

IS : 9509 - 1980
0.5 The volume of effluent and its pollution load vary considerably from These variations are due to various causes, principal plant to plant. among which are housekeeping, condition of plant and machinery, mode In view of this, the Committee has of their operation, and water use. refrained from incorporating in this standatd cost figures of a treatment plant based on any particular process. It is intended that each plant will select the treatment process best suited to its local conditions. 0.6 The object of this standard is to provide guidelines to viscose rayon The standard does not seek to provide units for treatment of effluents. detailed information on the working of a unit or on the designing and Further, the methods operation of the effluent treatment plant. recommended for adoption have been selected taking into consideration the practicability of thier adoption by the industry. When better and more economic methods of treatment become available, revision of this standard will be taken up. 0.7 It is recommended that plant located near the sea may preferably discharge their effluents into the marine coastal areas rather than into inland surface water. The extent of pollution of marine coastal areas permitted by discharge of effluents is laid down in IS : 7967-1976". 0.8 The extent of pollution of inland surface waters permitted by discharge of effluents is laid down in IS : 2296-19747. IS : 9509 - 1980 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers methods of treatment and disposal of eflluents of viscose rayon industry. It is a compilation of available data and information on sources, nature, volumes and pollutional effects of the effluents, ways of waste prevention and methods of their treatment and disposal. 2. DESCRIPTION 2.1 Plant Layout of the following: OF MANUFACTURING PROCESS

The layout of a modern viscose rayon plant consists

a) An acid plant for producing sulphuric acid, b) Carbon disulphide plant, c) The viscose processing units, d) Water treatment plant and softening plant, and e) Boiler house. 2.2 Raw Materials - The raw viscose rayon consist of cellulose various process chemicals. The materials to produce one tonne of Sl

materials used in the manufacture of derived from wood pulp or cotton and average requirements of the main raw viscose rayon are as follows:

2.3 Process - The basic raw material in the manufacture of viscose rayon is alpha cellulose derived from either wood pulp or cotton linters. The cellulose is converted into alkali cellulose by steeping the raw material in a solution of caustic soda ( 18 to 20 percent m/v) to dissolve The alpha cellulose remains insoluble. The excess the hemicellulose. The alkali cellulose is allowed to alkali is squeezed out and recycled. ripen and then converted to cellulose xanthate by treatment with carbon disulphide. The xanthate is subsequently dissolved in dilute caustic soda solution ( 1.7 to 2.5 percent m/v ) to give a solution of proper 5

IS:9509-1980 The resulting solution, known as viscose, is separated by filter viscosity. The viscose pressing, deaerated and stored under controlled conditions. is extruded under pressure into fine jets, through numerous spinnerets into spinning bath containing dilute sulphuric acid ( 8 to 10 percent m/v), zinc sulphate (0.5 to 1 percent m/v), and certain other chemicals which are essential to the spinning process. 2.3.1 The spun yarn is first washed free of acid with copious water and then washed free of sulphur which is precipitated on it during its formation by treatment with an alkaline sodium sulphide solution. This is It is then bleached, followed by washing with copious volume of water. washed with dilute acid solution and detergents. The yarn passes through a final stage of finishing and drying and is then conditioned to requisite moisture content and packed for despatch. 3. 3.3.1 Acidic Wastes - The acidic waste water is a mixture of the spent spin bath, make up tanks and spinning machines, evaporator and washings. It has a low PH, high acidity, dissolved solids, sulphate and zinc. The sulphate is in the form of sodium sulphate and as sulphuric acid. The organic content of the acidic wastes is, however, quite low as seen from the biochemical oxygen demand and chemical oxygen demand values. Not withstanding its small volume this waste consist of the strongest and most highly toxic component of rayon wastes. 3.3.2 Alkaline Wastes - The alkaline waste water has a high PH, a variable total dissolved solids and suspended solids. 3.3.3 Characteristics of Combined Wastes - The characteristics of the composite mill wastes from a selected group of rayon manufacturing units in the country are shown in Table 3. The combined waste is generally acidic and has high total dissolved solids and low biochemical and chemical oxygen demand. Zinc is present in variable concentration, The sulphate content is high but often exceeding the permissible limits. the chloride content is low. 3.4 Pollution Load - The pollution load contributed by viscose rayon wastes is mostly in the form of inorganic chemicals like sulphuric acid, sodium sulphate, zinc sulphate and sodium sulphide. The organic constituent of the pollution load is however quite low as will be seen from the low biochemical and chemical oxygen demand of the waste The pollution load contributed by some ,of the major rayon water. units in the country is shown in Table 4.

4. POLLUTIONAL

EFFECTS may have

4.1 The effluents discharged by a viscose rayon factory adverse effects on the receiving streams in many ways.

4.1.1 Efect of Acidic Wastes - The free mineral acids present in the wastes are objectionable in a stream on account of corrosive action on metal, concrete structures and pumps. Acids will lower the /JH of the stream and liberate hydrogen sulphide from bottom deposits. There will be a suppression of biochemical activity in the stream and retardation of bacterial self purification. Increase in hydrogen ion concentration ( lowering of pH value ) will be injurious to fish life through precipitation and coagulation of the secretion of the gills and gill membranes. 4.1.2 Effects of Alkaline Wastes - The alkaline wastes having PH greater than 9.0 can be lethal to all forms of aquatic life. 10

4.1.3 Toxic Effects due to <inc - Zinc is highly toxic to fish. The lethal concentration of zinc to fish life varies according to the species. The concentration of zinc is the combined rayon wastes is often greater than the threshold limits.

4.1.4 Oxygen Depletion - Depletion of dissolved oxygen in the streams may result from the organic substances and sulphide present in the waste. 11

IS : 9509 - 1980 5. METHODS 5.1 Treatment 5.1.1 OF TREATMENT of rayon factory wastes consists of the following. by recovery of process chemicals. for self or alkali

Reduction

in waste strength

5.1.2 Equalization of acidic and alkaline waste streams neutralization and supplemented by treatment with either acid for pH correction to the desired limits. 5.1.3 5.1.4 Primary Secondary Treatment Treatmenl

5.2 Reduction of Waste Strength - The first essential step towards treatment of the wastes consists in the reduction of waste strength by The acidic and alkaline process wastes recovery of process chemicals. are segregated from each other and are treated independently for byproduct recovery. From the alkaline wastes caustic soda is recovered by From the highly concentrated acidic spent dialysis and recycled. spinbath solution and washings, sodmm sulphate and zinc can be Sodium sulphate is obtained by concentration, evaporation recovered. and crystallization. Recovery of zinc is made by either chemical precipitation with caustic soda at a critical pH of -9.0, as zinc hydroxide, followed by sedimentation and filtration or by ion exchange `process. The chemical recovery is an integral point of the unit processes in the manufacture of viscose rayon. 5.3 Equalization of the Waste - The acidic and aikaline wastes are mixed in an equalization tank and requisite amount of lime is added for pH correction. 5.4 Primary waste stream 5.4.1 5.4.2 5.4.3 Treatment -The primary consists of the following steps. of the waste for removal of coarse gritty of suspended materials. solids by settling. treatment of the combined

Screening Removal Removal

of coarse floating

matter.

and settleable

5.5 Secondary Treatment - The treatment of the wastes for reduction in biochemical oxygen demand can be carried out in a conventional The biochemical oxygen demand of aerobic waste treatment system. the combined waste is quite low (50 to 100 mg/l ). In some of the viscose rayon factories wherein rayon grade wood pulp is also produced, 12

IS : 9509 - 1980 the waste stream is likely to have a high biochemical oxygen demand ( 300 to 700 mg/l ). Even so the wastes could be successfully treated by conventional aerobic systems of which the trickling filter with recirculation has been found to be most suitable by the rayon industry in UK and USA. The wastes can also be treated more economically by low cost waste treatment systems, preferably the aerated lagoon. The composite wastes are deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus and they can be easily provided in the system as supplementary nutrients. More advantageously the viscose rayon process wastes can also be treated in combination with domestic sewage. 6. METHODS RECOMMENDED FOR ADOPTION IN INDIA

6.1 Reviewing the methods outlined in 5, it is recommended that a scheme for complete treatment of composite effluents from viscose rayon industries would consist of the following. 6.1.1 Segregation of the various process waste streams.

6.1.2 Equalization of the acidic and alkaline waste streams for self neutralization with provision for further treatment with lime if pH correction to the requisite degree is found necessary. 6.1.3 Primary treatment for removal of floating matter, oil and grease and suspended and settleable solids. 6.1.4 Secondary aerobic treatment for biochemical oxygen demand reduction either by conventional trickling filter and activated sludge process or low cost systems like an aerated lagoon or oxidation pond. 6.2 It may be stated that the degree of treatment to be provided by a particular factory will be determined by the ultimate disposal of the effluents into the environment, that is, discharge into public sewers, surface streams or directly into the sea. 6.3 For discharge into municipal sewers, the treatment may be limited to the primary stage only; and for discharge into inland surface waters, secondary treatment for biochemical oxygen demand reduction will be The degree of dilution available in the stream will be yet necessary. another factor to be considered. 6.4 For disposal in the marine environment, the degree of treatment will In view be determined by the prescribed standards of effluent quality. of the considerable degree of dilution available, the effluents from viscose rayon manufacture may be discharged into the sea after primary 13

1s : 9509 - 1980 treatment. This would require a well designed submarine outfall system with suitable arrangements.for efficient diffusion and dispersion of the effluents from the outfall system into the sea. 6.5 The secondary treatment a) Lagooning; aerobic treatment including trickling filter, b) Coventional activated sludge process; and/or c) Low cost waste treatment like aerated lagoon and the oxidation pond. 6.5.1 FIow sheet of a treatment plant is shown in Fig. 2. consists of the following:
